module restoring_divider (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input start,
    input [4:0] dividend,
    input [2:0] divisor,
    output reg [4:0] quotient,
    output reg [2:0] remainder,
    output reg done
);
    reg [4:0] A; // Accumulator
    reg [4:0] Q; // Quotient
    reg [2:0] R; // Remainder
    reg [2:0] count; // Count for the number of bits processed
    reg state; // State variable (0 for idle, 1 for division)
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            A <= 0;
            Q <= 0;
            R <= 0;
            quotient <= 0;
            remainder <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            count <= 0;
            state <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // Idle state
                    if (start) begin
                        A <= dividend; // Load dividend
                        Q <= 0; // Reset quotient
                        R <= divisor; // Load divisor
                        count <= 5; // Set count to number of bits
                        state <= 1; // Move to division state
                    end
                    done <= 0;
                end
                1: begin // Division state
                    if (count > 0) begin
                        // Left Shift
                        A <= {A[3:0], Q[4]}; // Concatenate for next bit
                        Q <= {Q[3:0], 1'b0}; // Shift quotient left
                        
                        // Subtract
                        if (A >= R) begin
                            A <= A - R; // Subtract divisor
                            Q[0] <= 1; // Set LSB of quotient
                        end
                        count <= count - 1; // Decrement count
                    end else begin
                        quotient <= Q; // Output quotient
                        remainder <= A; // Output remainder
                        done <= 1; // Indicate done
                        state <= 0; // Go back to idle
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire [7:0] dst_addr,
    input wire [15:0] data_in1,
    input wire [15:0] data_in2,
    output reg [15:0] data_out,
    output reg done
);

    localparam IDLE = 2'b00, TRANSFER = 2'b01, DONE = 2'b10;

        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                done <= 0;
                if (start) begin
                    state <= TRANSFER;
                end

                if (channel_select == 1'b0) begin
                    data_out <= data_in1; // Transfer from channel 1
                end else begin
                    data_out <= data_in2; // Transfer from channel 2
                end
                state <= DONE;
            end
            DONE: begin
                done <= 1;
                state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle after completion
            end
        endcase
    end
endmodule

    output reg [3:0] crc_out

    input reset,
    input start,
    input miso,
    output reg mosi,
    output reg sclk,
    output reg ss
);
    reg [3:0] state;
    reg [7:0] data_out;
    reg [7:0] data_in;
    reg [2:0] bit_cnt;

    localparam IDLE      = 4'b0000,
               START     = 4'b0001,
               SEND      = 4'b0010,
               RECEIVE    = 4'b0011,
               STOP      = 4'b0100;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            mosi <= 1'b0;
            sclk <= 1'b0;
            ss <= 1'b1; // Active low
            bit_cnt <= 3'b000;
            data_in <= 8'b0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    ss <= 1'b1; // Slave deselected
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= START;
                        ss <= 1'b0; // Select the slave
                    end
                end

                START: begin
                    state <= SEND;
                    bit_cnt <= 3'b000;
                end

                SEND: begin
                    if (bit_cnt < 3'b1000) begin // 8 bits
                        sclk <= 1'b1; // Clock high
                        mosi <= data_out[bit_cnt]; // Send data
                        bit_cnt <= bit_cnt + 1;
                        state <= RECEIVE;
                    end else begin
                        state <= STOP;
                    end
                end

                RECEIVE: begin
                    sclk <= 1'b0; // Clock low
                    if (bit_cnt <= 3'b1000) begin
                        data_in[bit_cnt - 1] <= miso; // Receive data
                    end
                    state <= SEND; // Go back to send the next bit
                end

                STOP: begin
                    ss <= 1'b1; // Deselect the slave
                    state <= IDLE;
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a 2-channel DMA (Direct Memory Access) controller that allows for transferring data from a source memory to a destination memory. The controller should manage two channels, where each channel can be activated independently. The DMA controller should have the following inputs and outputs:
- Inputs:
  - clk: Clock signal
  - rst: Reset signal (active high)
  - channel_1_start: Start signal for channel 1 (active high)
  - channel_2_start: Start signal for channel 2 (active high)
  - source_address_1: 8-bit source address for channel 1
  - destination_address_1: 8-bit destination address for channel 1
  - source_address_2: 8-bit source address for channel 2
  - destination_address_2: 8-bit destination address for channel 2
  - data: 8-bit data to be transferred
- Outputs:
  - channel_1_done: Indicator that channel 1 has completed the transfer (active high)
  - channel_2_done: Indicator that channel 2 has completed the transfer (active high)
The DMA controller should transfer data for a fixed number of cycles (e.g., 4 cycles) for each channel once the start signal is received. After the transfer is complete, the done signal for that channel should be asserted high for one clock cycle.

module dma_controller (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input channel_1_start,
    input channel_2_start,
    input [7:0] source_address_1,
    input [7:0] destination_address_1,
    input [7:0] source_address_2,
    input [7:0] destination_address_2,
    input [7:0] data,
    output reg channel_1_done,
    output reg channel_2_done
);

    reg [2:0] state; // 0: idle, 1: transfer_channel_1, 2: transfer_channel_2, 3: done_channel_1, 4: done_channel_2
    reg [3:0] transfer_count; // Counts the number of cycles of transfer

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= 0;
            channel_1_done <= 0;
            channel_2_done <= 0;
            transfer_count <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // idle state
                    if (channel_1_start) begin
                        state <= 1; // start channel 1 transfer
                        transfer_count <= 0;
                    end else if (channel_2_start) begin
                        state <= 2; // start channel 2 transfer
                        transfer_count <= 0;
                    end
                end
                1: begin // transferring channel 1
                    // Transfer data logic for channel 1 here (skipped for simplicity)
                    transfer_count <= transfer_count + 1;
                    if (transfer_count == 4) begin
                        state <= 3; // done with channel 1
                    end
                end
                2: begin // transferring channel 2
                    // Transfer data logic for channel 2 here (skipped for simplicity)
                    transfer_count <= transfer_count + 1;
                    if (transfer_count == 4) begin
                        state <= 4; // done with channel 2
                    end
                end
                3: begin // done channel 1
                    channel_1_done <= 1;
                    state <= 0; // go back to idle
                end
                4: begin // done channel 2
                    channel_2_done <= 1;
                    state <= 0; // go back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit serializer that takes 8 bits of input data and serializes it into a single output bit stream, one bit at a time, at each clock cycle. The serializer should have a load signal to load the data into the serializer and a start signal to begin the serialization process. The output should be valid on each clock cycle after the start signal is asserted.
code:
module serializer (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input load,
    input start,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg serial_out,
    output reg done
);
    reg [2:0] bit_count; // To count the number of bits serialized
    reg [7:0] shift_reg; // Shift register to hold data

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            bit_count <= 3'b000;
            shift_reg <= 8'b00000000;
            serial_out <= 1'b0;
            done <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (load) begin
                shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data into the shift register
                bit_count <= 3'b000;   // Reset bit count
                done <= 1'b0;          // Reset done signal
            end else if (start && bit_count < 3'b1000) begin
                serial_out <= shift_reg[7]; // Output the most significant bit
                shift_reg <= shift_reg << 1; // Shift left to prepare the next bit
                bit_count <= bit_count + 1;   // Increment bit count
            end
            
            if (bit_count == 3'b111) begin
                done <= 1'b1; // Set done signal when all bits are serialized
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    output reg timeout
);

            timeout <= 0;

        end
    end
